sentences.text: Storage allocation begins after the shipment count, inspection status, and door release have been recorded.
The Warehouse Management System evaluates available positions against pallet dimensions, mass, storage compatibility, and expected retrieval demand.
Fast-moving inventory is generally assigned to positions that support short travel paths to its next handling step.
Pallets with restricted handling requirements are assigned only to positions approved for those conditions.
The allocation logic preserves clearances for the pallet and the equipment needed to access it.
A position is excluded when its capacity, status, or operating restrictions conflict with the pallet profile.
The Warehouse Management System produces the Slot Reservation Receipt.
A reservation remains subject to confirmation that the selected position and its access path are available for operation.
The reservation record identifies the selected position and the conditions used to validate its suitability.
Crane operations are divided into aisle zones to limit conflicting equipment movement.
Each stacker crane normally retrieves and stores pallets within its assigned aisle boundaries.
The North Aisle Stacker Crane is also known by the alias Juniperwake.
The North Aisle Stacker Crane serves storage positions in the north aisle and follows the aisle's configured travel limits.
The South Aisle Stacker Crane serves its assigned storage positions under equivalent travel and access controls.
Cross-aisle movement is controlled so that crane travel does not extend beyond authorized operating zones.
Crane commands are issued only when the target position and the required aisle conditions are valid.
The Pallet Dimension Scanner is also known by the alias Moonquarry.
The Pallet Dimension Scanner measures pallet height, width, and length before storage suitability is finalized.
The measured profile is checked against configured dimensional limits and the declared pallet profile.
The Pallet Dimension Scanner produces the Oversize Load Advisory.
The dimension advisory identifies a measured profile that exceeds an applicable storage or handling limit.
An advisory does not by itself authorize placement in a position that fails the storage rules.
The Warehouse Management System can retain the measured dimensions with the pallet's inventory record for later allocation decisions.
The Warehouse Operations Supervisor can review unresolved allocation conditions through established operational procedures.
